title: Progressive onboarding: guided pin flow with profile-compare panel
creator: Maya Chen
body:
Summary: Build a stepwise onboarding workflow in the Console that guides engineers through: (1) selecting a model and recommended version, (2) publishing and comparing performance profiles, and (3) creating a version pin with weighted traffic split for safe rollout. The flow should reduce cognitive overhead for first-time model owners and provide side-by-side profile comparisons (latency, throughput, token cost, quality regressions) when choosing a pin target.

Why: We continue to see customers delay version pinning because they cannot quickly evaluate trade-offs between latency/cost and quality. A guided flow plus an integrated profile-compare panel will increase pin adoption, reduce mispins, and make rollouts predictable. This also ties into our onboarding playbook for Dedicated/Private deployments where customers must pin versions explicitly.

Scope: Console UX and light backend support for running a comparison query set and surface summarized metrics. Minimum viable capabilities: guided stepper UI, profile-compare panel (3 profiles max), suggested pin configuration (immediate/canary/weighted), safety checks (compatibility matrix, missing KV cache), and telemetry for conversion rate.

Out of scope for this ticket: deep model quality evaluation engine, autoscaling policy changes, on-prem install automation.

Acceptance criteria:
- A 3-step onboarding modal is implemented in Console: Choose Model -> Compare Profiles -> Create Pin.
- Profile-compare panel shows: median latency, p95 latency, tokens/sec, per-token cost estimate, recent eval delta (quality), and a small heatmap for sequence-length sensitivity.
- Console suggests a default canary split (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and exposes a slider for weighted traffic.
- Safety checks block pin if model variant incompatible with customer's runtime settings and provide actionable guidance.
- Frontend has unit tests and end-to-end coverage for the main happy path.
- Telemetry events emitted for each step; conversion metrics are visible in the project dashboard.

Design links: Figma flow + mockups: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/console-pin-onboarding (internal), prototype: https://figma.prototype/pin-flow
PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONBOARD/Progressive+Pin+Flow
Engineering spike notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/eng/spikes/pin-profile-compare
design_notes: Design direction favors a compact, vertically stacked compare panel optimized for technical users. Each profile card uses a small badge for runtime (hosted/dedicated/private), an indicator for quantization, and a three-line summary: latency/cost/quality. Compare actions: expand to sequence-length distribution, open detailed profile page, or mark as 'baseline' for future regressions. Work with Design (DES-9140) to finalize microcopy for safety checks.
engineering_notes:
Backend: add a lightweight compare API that accepts up to 3 model-version ids and a canonical query-set id; returns aggregated metrics from TimeSeries store and last eval run. We will reuse existing perf-profile table and add a 'comparison_snapshot' view. Edge cases: missing recent eval -> show 'stale' badge and fallback to historical aggregate.
Frontend: implement Stepper with optimistic UI while comparison runs; show progress and allow users to continue to pin with a warning. Integrate with Rollouts service to create a weighted pin.
Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1428 (stepper first pass), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/992 (compare API prototype).
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (beta): enable for self-serve orgs with <100k tokens/day; collect telemetry and qualitative feedback from 5 pilot customers. Feature flag controlled.
Phase 2: open to all orgs, add more robust eval delta visualization and heatmaps.
Monitoring: dashboard for step-to-pin conversion, errors per org, time-to-compare. Rollback: feature flag off or revert to old version-picker flow.
open_questions: What is the canonical query-set we run for profile comparison in Hosted vs Dedicated? (Product/Research to decide)
Should we allow comparison of different model families (e.g., LP vs HF fork) or restrict to compatible architectures?
How will per-token cost be estimated for private deployments where cost model differs?
qa_testcases: Happy path: select model v1, compare with v2, create a 5% canary pin, verify traffic split and metrics recorded.
Stale eval: compare shows stale badge and warning; engineer can still pin after acknowledging risk.
Safety block: attempt pin with incompatible runtime (missing KV cache) and verify blocking message and remediation steps.
Telemetry: verify events emitted for step_enter, step_complete, compare_requested, pin_created with org and user ids.
Edge case: compare API times out -> UI shows partial metrics and allows user to retry or proceed with warning.
updates: 2026-02-22 - Maya Chen: Kickoff with Design and Eng. Agreed scope for MVP and measurement goals.
2026-03-01 - Luca Alvarez: Spike complete. Backend compare API prototype returns aggregated metrics for 3 versions. PR opened (runtime#992).
2026-03-04 - Priya Nair (Research): Provided recommended canonical query-set for Hosted; suggested lightweight eval suite of 25 inference prompts. See research notes link.
2026-03-07 - Design review: DES-9140 delivered initial mocks; requested smaller cards and clearer 'stale' state.
notes_for_release: Ship behind FF: feature_flag.console.progressive_pin_flow. Include a migration job to mark current 'baseline' profile for orgs that don't select one. Communicate in release notes: 'Try guided model pinning with side-by-side performance comparisons'.
